_documentation: Lighthouse CI assertion config for .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml (#270). Category thresholds sit below the day-to-day scores on purpose: the gate exists to catch collapses (a 1 MB image landing on a page, a render-blocking regression), not to flake on shared-runner variance. The performance floor is 0.70: the heaviest audited page (about.html, a long page with the deliverables Gantt + self-hosted fonts) measured a median 0.72 on the GitHub runner on 2026-07-16, after the July 2026 editorial pass first dropped it to a flapping 0.69-0.70 (#1355) and the reveal-animation exemption on page headers in #1352 won the margin back. The 2-point headroom is thin, so if flapping returns the next levers are trimming render-blocking site.css or a 0.65 floor (see #1355 for the analysis). A first 0.75 floor flaked on about.html at 0.74 in an earlier era. resource-summary:image:size warns when any audited page ships more than 500 KB of images, the class of regression the June 2026 press-kit fix removed. The workflow is not a required check, so a red run signals without blocking auto-merge. Two things were settled in #1613. Every assertion now sets aggregationMethod explicitly, because the Lighthouse CI default is `optimistic`: for a minScore that means the assertion runs against the BEST of the three runs, and for a maxNumericValue against the SMALLEST, so every threshold here used to be measured at its luckiest moment rather than its typical one (confirmed in @lhci/utils 0.15.1, src/assertions.js line 139). And the performance floor moved from 0.70 to 0.78, because #1617 replaced `python3 -m http.server` (HTTP/1.0, no gzip, no ranges) with scripts/serve-static.cjs, which behaves like GitHub Pages. That lifted every page by 9 to 16 points, so 0.70 had stopped gating anything. 0.78 sits three points under the worst median measured across two samples on main (about.html at 0.82 and 0.81), which is the same headroom the old 0.70 had against its own worst page. Despite being a higher number this is a stricter gate than before, since it now fails when a page genuinely degrades instead of passing on one lucky run in three. network-map.html held the one exemption this config ever needed, dropping categories:seo while the page carried a deliberate noindex as an unlisted prototype. #1598 signposted the page and removed the noindex, and the first measured run afterwards put it at seo 1.00 against the 0.90 floor, so the exemption and the assertMatrix it forced both went away in #1605. Every audited page is now held to the same assertions.
